### Institution penalty

There are eight world-changing ideas that spread throughout the world over the course of history. Societies that haven't embraced these ideas will have a harder time keeping up in technology as the rest of the world, especially Europe where these ideas usually originate, outpaces them. Each technology has specific institution requirements, which will increase tech cost by +15%, +30% or +50% when not fulfilled, and give a corresponding bonus to the maximum number of stockpiled monarch points. These penalties accumulate as additional institutions appear; at the extreme, a country that still hasn't embraced any institution in 1821 will have a +400% penalty to technology cost.

### General modifiers

General modifiers reduce the cost of all technology types.

# Institutions

**Institutions** are fundamental advances in civilization and are the primary determinant of technology cost. Technologies require specific institutions to be embraced and will have increased tech cost penalties otherwise (as shown through the icons above the technology, where those shown in red or grayed out are increasing the cost). The first tech of an institution receives an institution penalty of +15% the next one +30% and all following techs +50%. This penalty can stack if multiple institutions are not embraced.

Embracing an institution requires that institution to be fully present in provinces containing at least 10% of a country's development (modified by local autonomy), after which it requires an amount of ducats dependent on the remaining development in provinces where the institution is not fully present.

There are a total of 8 different institutions that appear throughout the game (except for the first which is present at the beginning of the game in 1444), at roughly 50-year intervals starting in 1450 and ending in 1750.

Each year all provinces an institution can spawn in are randomly given a chance to spawn the institution. Each eligible province for an institution has a fixed chance (5% to 100% depending on the institution) to get it to spawn in that province. ## Why Is Your Tech So Expensive in India?

There are **two layered causes**, and for an Indian nation both are usually hitting you at once.

---

### 1. 🏛️ Un-embraced Institutions — The #1 Culprit

This is almost always the real answer. «Institutions» (wiki) explains it clearly:

> *"The first tech of an institution receives a penalty of +15%, the next +30%, and all following techs +50%. This penalty stacks across multiple un-embraced institutions."*

There are **8 institutions** total (Feudalism, Renaissance, Colonialism, Printing Press, Global Trade, Manufactories, Enlightenment, Industrialization), appearing roughly every 50 years from 1450 onward. **They almost always spawn in Western Europe first** and spread outward slowly. As an Indian nation, you are far from the origin point — institutions reach you late, or you must actively spread them yourself.

The math gets brutal fast:

| Un-embraced Institutions | Extra Tech Cost |
|---|---|
| 1 | up to **+50%** per tech level |
| 2 | up to **+100%** |
| 3 | up to **+150%** |
| All 8 ignored until 1821 | **+400%** (!) |

So if your tech feels impossibly expensive mid-game, **open the tech screen and look at the institution icons above the tech buttons** — red/greyed icons = you're paying those penalties right now.

---

### 2. 🌏 Indian Tech Group — Starting Penalty

The «Technology» (wiki) table confirms:

> *Indian tech group: **+50% starting institution penalty***

This means many Indian nations begin the game **without Feudalism already embraced**, so you start at a 50% penalty even on day 1 (unlike Western nations who start with Feudalism and pay no extra cost until Renaissance appears). The specific nations listed include Bastar, Chanda, Garha, Ladakh, Manipur, Tripura, and others.

---

### 3. ⏳ Time-Based Cost Increase

A smaller additional factor: tech cost rises **linearly over the game**, up to **+30% by 1821**, purely based on how historically late the current tech level was discovered. This applies to everyone, but it compounds your other penalties.

---

### ✅ How to Fix It

| Problem | Solution |
|---|---|
| Institutions not spreading to India | **Manually spread them**: send a merchant or diplomat to get them into your provinces, or develop a province where the institution exists |
| Can't afford to embrace yet | Embrace as soon as the institution is **≥10% present** in your development — the ducats to embrace are far cheaper than the ongoing monarch point drain from the tech penalty |
| Behind on tech despite embracing | Use the **neighbor bonus**: you get **−5% tech cost per level you're behind** the most advanced nation bordering you (up to −75%). A Western nation bordering your territory actually helps you! |
| Still struggling | Take ideas that reduce tech cost (e.g. **Innovative** idea group gives −10% tech cost) |

**The bottom line:** Check your institutions screen first. If you're 2–3 institutions behind and haven't embraced them, you could be paying **100–150% extra** on every tech purchase. Embracing institutions is the single highest-impact action you can take.

*Sources: «Technology» (wiki), «Institutions» (wiki), «Growth Engine» (fundamentals)*
